question.problem: On a shelf, there are $12$ action movie DVDs and $8$ cartoon DVDs. A man randomly selects $3$ DVDs from the shelf. What is the probability that he has chosen $2$ action movie DVDs and $1$ cartoon DVD? Round your answer to the nearest percent.
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ represent the event described in the question. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{n}{N},\end{aligned}
$$

where $N$ is the total number of ways to pick $3$ DVDs out of $20,$ and $n$ is the number of ways to choose exactly $2$ action movie DVDs and $1$ cartoon DVD. 

Since the order in which he picks the DVDs does not matter, we use combinations.

First, we compute $N.$ The number of ways to pick $3$ DVDs from a total of $20$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}N={}_{20}{C}_{3} & =\frac{20!}{3!\cdot 17!}=1140.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $n.$ The computation of $n$ can be divided into two steps: 

- the number of ways to choose $2$ (out of $12$) action movie DVDs is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{C}_{2}=\frac{12!}{2!\cdot 10!}=66.\end{aligned}
$$

- the number of ways to choose $1$ (out of $8$) cartoon DVD is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{8}{C}_{1} & =\frac{8!}{1!\cdot 7!}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the results from the above steps, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n={}_{12}{C}_{2}\cdot {}_{8}{C}_{1}=66\cdot 8=528.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{528}{1140}≈0.46=46%.\end{aligned}
$$
